question: What physical property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
explanation: Frequency measures the speed of wave cycles, which directly corresponds to the perceived pitch of a sound. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h1)

question: How does the ear function as a biological transducer?

options.A: It converts mechanical sound energy into electrical nerve impulses
options.B: It changes air pressure directly into cerebrospinal fluid waves
options.C: It amplifies high-frequency waves into thermal energy
options.D: It filters out background noise using chemical buffers

explanation: Transduction involves changing one form of energy into another, which the ear accomplishes by turning physical sound waves into neural signals. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which structure connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx?
explanation: The Eustachian tube equalizes pressure between the middle ear and the atmosphere by connecting to the nasopharynx. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h2)

question: What are the three bones of the middle ear called collectively?
explanation: The malleus, incus, and stapes are known as the auditory ossicles. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why does the middle ear act as an impedance-matching transformer?

options.A: To convert high-frequency sounds into low-frequency vibrations
options.B: To prevent energy loss when sound moves from air to fluid
options.C: To equalize the blood pressure inside the temporal bone
options.D: To cool down the inner ear fluids during high-intensity noise

explanation: Fluid offers more resistance to sound waves than air does, requiring mechanical amplification by the ossicles to transfer energy efficiently. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which bone of the middle ear directly contacts the oval window?
explanation: The footplate of the stapes fits directly into the oval window to transmit vibrations into the inner ear. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h3)

question: Where do pressure waves in the cochlea ultimately dissipate?
explanation: The round window acts as a pressure relief valve for the fluid-filled chambers of the cochlea. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h4)

question: How are different sound frequencies mapped along the basilar membrane?

options.A: Frequencies are sorted by amplitude rather than location on the membrane
options.B: All frequencies stimulate the entire membrane with equal intensity
options.C: High frequencies peak near the base, low frequencies peak near the apex
options.D: High frequencies peak near the apex, low frequencies peak near the base

explanation: The stiffness and width gradient of the basilar membrane causes high pitches to register at the stiff base and low pitches at the flexible apex. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the name of the sensory receptors responsible for hearing?
explanation: Hair cells within the Organ of Corti contain stereocilia that transduce mechanical movement into electrical signals. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h5)

question: What triggers the opening of ion channels in the stereocilia during hearing?

options.A: Electrical discharge from nearby bone cells
options.B: Chemical binding of hormones in the fluid
options.C: Mechanical bending caused by motion against the tectorial membrane
options.D: Thermal expansion of fluid during loud noise

explanation: The movement of the basilar membrane creates a shearing force that physically bends the stereocilia, opening mechanically gated ion channels. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which cranial nerve transmits auditory impulses from the inner ear to the brain?
explanation: The vestibulocochlear nerve carries both hearing and balance signals from the inner ear to the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary function of the superior olivary complex in the auditory pathway?

options.A: Storing long-term memory of spoken words
options.B: Converting electrical signals back into mechanical fluid waves
options.C: Filtering out background noise before it reaches the thalamus
options.D: Localizing sound by comparing timing and intensity from both ears

explanation: The superior olivary complex is the first place in the brain where auditory information from both ears converges to help determine sound direction. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h6)

question: In which lobe of the brain is the primary auditory cortex located?
explanation: The temporal lobe houses the auditory cortex, which handles conscious perception and interpretation of sounds. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h7)

question: What does tonotopic organization in the auditory cortex mean?

options.A: Loud sounds are processed in the left hemisphere and soft sounds in the right
options.B: All sound volumes are processed equally across the cortex
options.C: Musical tones are stored separately from spoken language
options.D: Specific cortical neurons respond preferentially to specific sound frequencies

explanation: Tonotopy preserves the frequency map of the cochlea all the way through to the primary auditory cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h7)
